A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Jr. AI Scientist study, and their text, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison. The 37 generated-paper pages, including embedded author comments, are identical; v3 adds supplementary material before them.

before.justification: V1 reports original DeepReviewer evaluations of generated papers in Table 2, author audits, and observed failures from developing and running the system.

after.justification: V3 retains those empirical evaluations and adds review-score distributions across all 18 generated papers before author selection in Section 4.2 and Figure 5.

M1.justification: The baseline-guided idea generation, experimental implementation and improvement, ablation, and manuscript-writing procedures remain unchanged. Appendix B documents prompts and operational details for these existing components; it does not establish a revised algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use LoCoOp and GL-MCM for out-of-distribution detection and Min-K%++ for pre-training data detection. The datasets and tasks in the generated-paper appendices are unchanged. Evaluating additional generated manuscripts does not introduce another domain or task scenario.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains AI Scientist-v1, AI Scientist-v2, AI-Researcher, CycleResearcher-12B and Zochi, with unchanged comparator membership. Comparisons inside the generated papers are also unchanged. Additional baselines suggested by the newly reproduced conference reviews were not newly evaluated.

E3.justification: V3 adds an evaluation of the complete 18-manuscript pool before author selection, alongside the retained three-paper selected comparison. This broadens the evaluated sample and explicitly examines selection effects. The newly specified six outputs per baseline and selection criteria do not establish an increased generation budget or rerunning of existing experiments.

E4.justification: Section 4.2 adds an analysis of selection effects and score reliability, including higher-scoring LoCoOp manuscripts that contained more hallucinations. Appendix C supplies detailed evidence from previously summarized conference-review cases. The generated-paper ablations and the existing development-risk case studies remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Figure 5 newly reports per-baseline score distributions over six generated outputs each, exposing output variability beyond v1's selected-paper averages and extrema. This adds descriptive variability reporting, without introducing confidence intervals, significance tests or explicit seed information, and without establishing additional generation runs.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and the generated-paper results are unchanged. V3 adds the mean score of 5.30 across all 18 outputs before selection, versus the retained 5.75 for the three selected papers, and identifies their scores as LoCoOp 6, GL-MCM 5 and Min-K%++ 6.25. Appendix C also adds individual conference-review scores for explicitly different, earlier system outputs.

T1.justification: The mathematical content of the generated papers and the GL-MCM pseudocode are retained. V3 introduces no new formal assumptions, derivations, propositions or proofs; the added prompts and reviewer criticisms do not constitute theoretical developments.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain baseline-guided autonomous research with multi-file code, higher DeepReviewer ratings, and an empirical risk report. V3 names DeepReviewer explicitly in the abstract and highlights the existing three demonstrations, while retaining the same substantive contribution and superiority claims in the introduction and conclusion.

C2.justification: V3 adds explicit limitations concerning untested combinations of coding agents and the fragility of Semantic Scholar novelty verification. Its selection analysis further explains why higher review scores need not indicate fewer hallucinations. The original warning against using the system to write submission papers is retained and expanded in the Broader Impact Statement.

D1.justification: Appendix B substantially expands reproducibility documentation with actual prompts, memory fields, file and output contracts, revision instructions, and the writing agent's CLAUDE.md. V3 also specifies reviewer hardware, a monthly cost option, and human preparation and selection details. Appendix A newly explains the planned gradual code release; it does not establish that a complete codebase is available.

R1.justification: V3 adds literature on broader scientific agents, automated reviewing and empirical failure analysis, including Kosmos, Denario and Luo et al. It sharpens the distinction from DeepScientist around workflow documentation and risk reporting. These are targeted expansions of the existing positioning; the OpenScholar publication update represents the same cited work.

P1.justification: The main Sections 1–8 retain their order and largely their wording. V3 makes localized explanatory rewrites, adds Limitations and Future Work and Broader Impact sections, and organizes supplementary material into Appendices A–D. The original generated papers are relocated without rewriting.

P2.justification: V3 adds the three-panel score-distribution Figure 5 and redraws Figure 2 with explicit stage-grouping boxes. It adopts TMLR front matter, headers and typography, and boxed prompt/review displays. Existing table structures, most diagrams and all generated-paper appendix layouts remain substantially intact.

improvement.justification: V3 improves transparency by documenting the selection pool and reporting its 5.30 mean alongside the selected papers' 5.75, making selection effects assessable. The detailed prompts and reproduced conference reviews also improve auditability. These gains are meaningful but limited: the main comparative results and three-baseline coverage remain unchanged, and the code release is still described as planned.
